how-to-build-an-rfp-compliance-matrix.ht.text:
← RFP compliance matrix generator

How to build an RFP compliance matrix

A compliance matrix is a table with one row per requirement in a solicitation. It exists for one reason: a proposal that skips a mandatory requirement can be scored non-responsive before anyone reads how good the rest is. The matrix is how a team proves to itself that every shall has an answer.

Paste your RFP and get a first-pass matrix

The columns

ColumnWhat goes in it
IDA stable number (REQ-001). Reviewers refer to it in comments.
Source sectionWhere the requirement appears in the solicitation (3.2.1, L.4, Attachment B). Evaluators search by this.
RequirementThe sentence as written. Do not paraphrase; paraphrase is where obligations get softened.
OwnerOne named person, not a team.
Proposal sectionThe page or heading in your response that answers it.
StatusNot started, drafted, reviewed, done.
ComplianceFully, partially, or not compliant, with a note. Say "partially" in the matrix before the evaluator says it for you.

Finding the requirements

  • Read three parts separately: the instructions to offerors (how to respond), the statement of work (what to deliver), and the evaluation criteria (how you will be scored). Requirements hide in all three.
  • Mark the trigger words: shall, must, is required to, will (when the contractor is the subject). Treat should and preferred as desirable, and shall not as a prohibition.
  • Split lists. "The Contractor shall: (a) ...; (b) ...; (c) ..." is three requirements, each of which can be missed separately.
  • Ignore the buyer's own duties. "The County will evaluate proposals within 30 days" is not yours to answer.
  • Pull instructions out separately. Page limits, fonts, copies, forms, the due date and the question deadline apply to the whole package. Check them once, at the end, with a fresh pair of eyes.

Mistakes that cost bids

  • Answering the scope and forgetting the forms: signed certifications, addendum acknowledgements, a notarised affidavit.
  • Counting pages after the layout changed, or using a smaller font than the instructions allow.
  • Treating a sentence with two obligations as one row.
  • Reading only the statement of work, when a requirement sits in the instructions or an attachment.
  • Not re-running the matrix after an addendum changes the text.

Doing the first pass in seconds

Typing a hundred rows is the part nobody enjoys. The free extractor does the first pass in your browser: it keeps the section number, splits lists, separates prohibitions and desirables, drops the buyer's duties, and exports a CSV with Owner and Status columns ready for the team. It is a heuristic, so check its output against the document. Nothing is uploaded, and there is a command-line version (see the README in the repository) for your own machine.

Before the matrix: should you bid at all?

The matrix is worth building once you have decided to bid. For the earlier go/no-go on deadlines, bonds, insurance and licences, use the tender bid readiness checker, and to find tenders worth reading, Tender Radar.

Common questions

What columns should an RFP compliance matrix have?

At minimum: a requirement ID, the solicitation section it comes from, the requirement text, who owns the response, the proposal section that answers it, and a status. Many teams add a compliance level (fully, partially, not compliant) and a notes column for assumptions.

How do I find every requirement in an RFP?

Read the instructions to offerors, the statement of work and the evaluation criteria separately. Mark every sentence with shall, must, is required to, or a contractor-subject will, split lists into one row per item, and keep prohibitions and desirable (should) items distinct from mandatory ones.

What makes a proposal non-responsive?

Commonly: missing a mandatory requirement, exceeding a page limit, missing a signed form or an addendum acknowledgement, submitting late or through the wrong channel. Rules vary by buyer, so read the instructions to offerors for the consequences of each.

Proposal teams · private browser tool · free

Turn an RFP into a compliance matrix

Paste the solicitation. Get a row for every shall, must and required statement, with its section number, a category, and Owner / Status / Proposal-section columns ready to fill in. Page limits, due dates, copies and required forms are pulled out separately. Download it as a spreadsheet.

Nothing is uploaded. Extraction runs on this device.

Compliance matrix

Owner and Status edited here are not saved or included in the download; the CSV has blank Owner and Not started columns for your team to fill in the spreadsheet.

Proposal instructions found

Check these once, at the end: they apply to the whole proposal rather than to a section.

TypeSectionText

Read this first

    Check your draft against the matrix

    Paste your draft proposal response (cite requirement IDs like REQ-004 if you can). The tool lists the requirements your draft does not seem to address yet. It compares key terms, so it finds gaps to look at; it cannot tell you a requirement is satisfied.

    IDStrengthStatusRequirementTerms not found

    What it does, and what it leaves to you

    • Finds: shall / must / is required to / will (when the contractor is the subject) obligations, shall-not prohibitions and should-style desirables, each with the sentence it came from. Lists introduced by "The Contractor shall:" become one row per item. Repeated sentences are merged.
    • Leaves out: the buyer's own duties ("the County will evaluate...").
    • Not decided: whether you can meet a requirement, whether a requirement is reasonable or lawful, evaluation weighting, or anything in a table, image or attachment you did not paste. Read the solicitation and every addendum.

    Prefer the command line? node cli.mjs rfp.txt --format csv > matrix.csv runs the same code on your own machine (see the README in the repository). Teams can also deploy their own copy with an API and an optional AI pass that splits compound requirements, using their own keys.

    Common questions

    What is an RFP compliance matrix?

    A compliance matrix is a table with one row per requirement in a solicitation: where the requirement appears, what it says, who answers it, where in the proposal it is answered, and whether it is done. Proposal managers use it to make sure no shall or must statement goes unanswered, because a missed mandatory requirement can make a proposal non-responsive.

    How does the generator find the requirements?

    It splits the pasted text into sentences, keeps the section number each sits under, and flags sentences with shall, must, is required to, will (when the contractor is the subject) and similar wording. It separates prohibitions (shall not), desirables (should) and the buyer's own duties (the County will). A lead-in such as The Contractor shall followed by a list becomes one row per list item.

    Is it as good as reading the RFP?

    No. It is a first pass that saves the typing. A sentence can contain two obligations, and requirements can hide in tables, figures and attachments that were not pasted. Read the whole solicitation and every addendum yourself, and check the matrix against it.

    Is my RFP uploaded anywhere?

    No. The extraction runs in your browser and nothing is sent to a server. There is also a command-line version that runs on your own machine.

// Fictional sample solicitation used by the page's "Load example" button and the tests.
export const SAMPLE = `REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS 26-014: Records Management Platform
Example County (fictional)

SECTION 1. INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS
1.1 Proposals must be submitted through the County e-procurement portal no later than 3:00 p.m. on March 14, 2027.
1.2 Questions must be submitted by email no later than February 20, 2027.
1.3 A mandatory pre-proposal conference will be held on February 6, 2027 at the County Annex.
1.4 The technical volume shall not exceed 25 pages, set in 11-point Arial with 1-inch margins.
1.5 Offerors shall submit one original and three copies of the price volume.
1.6 Offerors should include a one-page executive summary.
1.7 The County will evaluate proposals within 30 days of the due date.

SECTION 2. SCOPE OF WORK
2.1 The Contractor shall provide a hosted records management system that supports retention schedules and legal holds.
2.2 The Contractor shall:
  (a) migrate all existing records from the legacy system;
  (b) provide role-based access control and an audit log of every record view; and
  (c) maintain 99.9% monthly availability.
2.3 The system must encrypt data at rest and in transit in accordance with NIST SP 800-53 moderate controls.
2.4 The Contractor shall not store County data outside the United States.
2.5 The system should integrate with the County's existing single sign-on.
2.6 The Contractor will submit a monthly status report to the County project manager within five business days of month end.

SECTION 3. QUALIFICATIONS
3.1 The Contractor is required to hold an active SAM.gov registration.
3.2 Offerors must provide three references for similar projects completed in the last five years.
3.3 The proposed project manager must have at least eight years of experience and a PMP certification.
3.4 The Contractor shall carry commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence.

SECTION 4. PRICING
4.1 Offerors shall submit a fixed-price proposal for implementation and a separate annual subscription fee.
4.2 The Contractor shall provide hourly rates by labor category for change requests.
4.3 The Contractor will submit a monthly status report to the County project manager within five business days of month end.
`;
